q: Carbohydrates that cannot be hydrolysed into simpler sugars are called
why: Monosaccharides are the simplest carbohydrate units and cannot be hydrolysed further.

q: Sucrose, a non-reducing disaccharide, on hydrolysis gives
why: Sucrose is a disaccharide of glucose and fructose joined so that no free reducing group remains.

q: In solution, glucose mainly exists as a cyclic structure in the form of a
why: Glucose predominantly cyclises into a six-membered pyranose ring in aqueous solution.

q: The bond joining two amino acids in a protein chain is called a
why: The -COOH of one amino acid reacts with the -NH2 of the next, releasing water and forming a peptide (amide) bond.

q: The alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet arrangements of a polypeptide chain describe its
why: Secondary structure refers to the regular, hydrogen-bonded folding patterns like alpha-helix and beta-sheet.

q: In the lock-and-key model of enzyme action, the region where the substrate binds is called the
why: The active site is the specific region of the enzyme that binds the substrate to form the enzyme-substrate complex.

q: A deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy (bleeding gums)?
why: Vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen synthesis, leading to scurvy with bleeding gums.

q: Which vitamins are fat-soluble and stored in the body?
why: Vitamins A, D, E and K dissolve in fats and are stored, unlike water-soluble B-complex and C which are excreted.

q: DNA differs from RNA in that DNA contains
o: Deoxyribose sugar and thymine (instead of uracil)
Only single strand, no base pairing
why: DNA has deoxyribose sugar and the base thymine, while RNA has ribose sugar and uracil instead.

q: In DNA base pairing, adenine pairs with
why: Complementary base pairing rules state adenine pairs with thymine (A-T), and guanine pairs with cytosine (G-C).
